svg.title: More token rows reuse the same projection weights
svg.desc: A BF16 projection maps 1024 input features to 4096 output features using 8 MiB of weights. One token row requires 8.39 million FLOPs and 8.399 million modeled bytes, about 1 FLOP per byte. A group of 128 rows requires 1.074 billion FLOPs and 9.699 million bytes, about 110.7 FLOPs per byte. On a hypothetical 100 TFLOP/s, 1 TB/s device, resource lower bounds change from a memory-dominated 8.399 microseconds to a compute-dominated 10.737 microseconds. These are calculations under a read-once model, not measured latencies.
svg.text: More rows reuse the same weight matrix
Y = XWᵀ · input width 1024 · output width 4096 · BF16 storage · multiply-add = 2 FLOPs
W [4096, 1024] is 8 MiB in either case
Traffic model: read weights and inputs once; write outputs once. Real DRAM traffic may differ.
Illustrative rates: 100 TFLOP/s compute and 1 TB/s bandwidth. Crossover = 100 FLOP/byte.
The larger resource time is a lower bound, not a prediction of observed execution time.
Not an A6000 specification or measurement. Launch costs, cache behavior, tiling, and utilization remain outside this model.
